200.description: Pending work; pulling does not acknowledge delivery

get.summary: The bell: a normally quiet WebSocket that only says "sync now"
get.description:
Optional accelerator for ordinary HTTPS sync (call-me-maybe#132). Upgrade to a WebSocket, sending the box token in `Authorization` as for every box endpoint. One socket per box: a newer one replaces the older. The service sends only the text frame `{"t":"sync"}` (see `BellSignal`), meaning "run your ordinary HTTPS sync now"; rings close together are merged, and the box should merge them too. The box sends only the text frame `ping`, about every 25 seconds, and gets `pong`; without a ping for 60 seconds the socket no longer counts as presence and may be closed. Anything else from the box closes the socket. Nothing on the socket is configuration, a command or authority; HTTPS sync stays authoritative, and polling continues, more slowly, while the socket is healthy.

Close codes on an established socket: `4001` replaced by a newer socket for the same box (reconnect only with ordinary backoff); `4002` heartbeat timeout (reconnect with backoff); `1008` unexpected message; `1009` message too big. A refused upgrade is an HTTP answer, as on every box endpoint: `401` `box_removed` means the box was removed and must enrol again, so do not reconnect until it has; `401` `unauthorized` and `403` `sync_required` mean the credential will not work, so do not retry before it changes.

101.description: Switching Protocols: the socket is open. Every server frame is a `BellSignal`.

401.description: Invalid box credential: `unauthorized`, or `box_removed` once an owner or co-owner has removed the box from its family account (the box must enrol again). Do not retry before the credential changes.

426.description: `upgrade_required`: only a WebSocket upgrade is served here

boxToken.description: A box token with sync capability; browser sessions are not box tokens.

role.description: Present only on the account's lobby pass book.

Absent: a directory book, shown on the handsets that select it and never read for admission. lobby-pass: the box's one lobby pass book, whose contacts skip the lobby; never selectable, never included, never shown in a directory, with no includes and up to 5000 contacts. Every other book keeps the 2000-contact limit.

afterhours.description: The schedule id an extension's afterhours names, or every id when it names several; the extension is quiet while any is active. One id is always sent as a string.

ConfigRejection.description: Present while the newest configuration on the box's disk is rejected by its validator; the box keeps its last good revision. Omitted once a valid configuration is accepted.

file.description: Base name of the rejected file, such as policy.toml.

message.description: The validation problem, with phone numbers, PINs and tokens redacted.

at.description: Unix milliseconds when the box first rejected this content.

boxName.description: The name the box suggests for itself: BOX_NAME, otherwise its hostname. Sent until one status report carrying it has been accepted for the box's current enrolment, then omitted, so a box enrolled before enrolment carried a name still supplies one. A suggestion only: the name the household sets on the account wins.

afterhours.description: One schedule id, or several; a list of one is sent as the string it means.
